conventions.convention: S is locally compact, second countable, and Hausdorff. Local compactness means each point has a compact neighbourhood. Local finiteness means finite mass on every compact subset.
Counting measures allow repeated locations and the empty configuration. Configuration and locally finite measure spaces carry sigma-algebras generated by all Borel-set evaluations.
Pois(λ) has finite parameter λ ≥ 0, with λ = 0 defined separately as the point mass at zero. A count on a set of infinite intensity is instead +∞ almost surely.
A Cox model includes a supplied probability kernel giving the conditional point-process law given the directing measure; it is a Poisson law of intensity μ for Pξ-almost every μ.
Deletion removes exactly one occurrence at x, on the measurable domain where μ({x}) ≥ 1; other occurrences at x remain.
General locally finite Poisson existence assumes countable choice and dependent choice through the countable product theorem. The explicit finite-intensity construction uses no choice principle.
Campbell, Laplace, Mecke, and Cox moment formulas use nonnegative measurable test functions and allow extended values. The variance conclusion requires the stated finite second-moment conditions.

load_bearing.statement: A point process on S is a measurable map from a probability space into the locally finite counting measures equipped with the sigma-algebra generated by Borel-set evaluation maps; multiplicities are allowed.

A Poisson point process with locally finite, sigma-finite intensity ν has independent counts on every finite disjoint Borel family, with Poisson parameters ν(B) when finite and count +∞ almost surely when ν(B) = ∞. A Cox model supplies a conditional probability kernel whose laws are Poisson with the directing intensities almost everywhere.

For every finite Borel measure ν on S a Poisson process exists. For λ = ν(S) > 0 its law is the push-forward of the Poisson-weighted mixture of (ν/λ) product laws on the finite tuple spaces under summation of Dirac masses; for λ = 0 it is the zero process. Every Poisson process with this finite intensity has the same law.

Let S be locally compact, second countable, and Hausdorff. There is an increasing sequence of compact subsets K_n such that their union for n ≥ 1 is S and every compact subset of S is contained in some K_n.
For finite λ ≥ 0 the Poisson masses sum to one; EN = λ, E[N(N−1)] = λ², E[N²] = λ² + λ, Var(N) = λ, and E[s^N] = exp(λ(s−1)) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 1.
D = {(x, μ): μ({x}) ≥ 1} is measurable in the product evaluation sigma-algebra, and R:D → N_lf(S), R(x, μ) = μ − δ_x, is measurable and removes one occurrence.
For a Poisson point process η with finite intensity ν and every nonnegative measurable h, E[∫ h(x,η) η(dx)] = ∫ E[h(x,η+δ_x)] ν(dx), as extended nonnegative integrals.
For a Poisson point process η with locally finite intensity ν and every nonnegative Borel f, E[η(f)] = ν(f) and E[η(f)²] = ν(f²) + ν(f)², as identities in [0,∞].
Point processes with the evaluation sigma-algebra have equal laws if every finite vector of Borel-set counts has the same distribution.

For a random locally finite Borel measure ζ, ν(B) = E[ζ(B)] is a measure; every nonnegative Borel integral ζ(f) is measurable and satisfies E[ζ(f)] = ∫ f dν. The mean measure is locally finite exactly when E[ζ(K)] is finite for every compact K.

seams_checked.note: Contextual page prerequisite. The assigned point-process definitions and proofs do not invoke compensator, filtration, unit-jump, or martingale hypotheses. The page explicitly excludes compensator theory.

Reviewed finite mixed-binomial, diffuse-simplicity, spatial likelihood, and Gibbs/Papangelou uses. Finite total intensities, the zero-intensity case, occurrence products, and measurable one-occurrence deletion match the suppliers.

The ordered-event-time lemma uses the finite scalar count law and evaluation-measurable point-process definition on (0,T]. It constructs the finite mixture and proves absence of ties separately; it does not infer simplicity from the general point-process definition.
